subject: System design briefing — agenda & assets
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.k@atlas.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: System design briefing — agenda & assets

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Atlas would like to schedule a focused system-design briefing with your infra/serving team to walk through the production topology, SLOs, and planned fallback strategies before our joint pilot. High-level asks from our side:

- A walkthrough of how Redwood routes requests across model variants and handles KV cache priming.
- Expected tail latencies for 4k/8k sequences under reserved capacity.
- Any model quantization/precision trade-offs you recommend for retrieval-heavy workloads.
- An outline of audit/logging hooks we can integrate with our observability stack.

We'd like a 60–75 minute session with folks who own runtime, routing, and security. Proposed week: Apr 11–15. Our first preference is Wed Apr 13 10:00–11:15 PT; alternative Thu Apr 14 9:00–10:15 PT.

I've attached a short overview of our current prod footprint to help ground the conversation.

Attachments: atlas_prod_overview.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

If those windows don't work for your team, please propose two alternatives and a draft agenda / pre-reads we can review.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Platform Lead, Atlas Systems
alice.k@atlas.com

--

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. We're happy to run the deep-dive. Draft agenda and pre-reads below; happy to iterate.

Draft agenda (60–75m):
1) 5m — Introductions & goals (Hannah)
2) 15m — Serving runtime overview: batching, KV cache, and kernel selection (Jonas)
3) 15m — Routing and fallback policies (Aditya)
4) 10m — Security, logging, and audit hooks (Laura)
5) 15–25m — Q&A + concrete pilot checklist (all)

Pre-reads (please skim prior to the call):
- Slides: Redwood system brief v2 (link + slide deck attached) — highlights runtime choices we plan to demo.
- Diagrams: Live sequence & cache flow (Figma) — covers KV caching and cache priming patterns.
- Ops note: Rollout & fallback runbook (Drive doc) — includes canary steps and SLO guardrails.

Links and assets: 
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExample
- Diagrams (Figma/InVision): https://redwood.invisionapp.com/diagrams/system-cache-flow
- Slide deck: redwood_system_brief_v2.pptx (attached)

Proposed slots (PT):
- Wed, Apr 13 10:00–11:15 (preferred)
- Thu, Apr 14 09:00–10:15 (alternate)

Please confirm which slot works and any additional folks you want on the call (SRE, product, etc.). We'll add the invite and a short runbook link for attendees.

Thanks — I'll own the agenda and we will circulate final pre-reads 48h before the session.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Quick internal note — agreed on the agenda. A couple of tactical asks from my side before we lock:

- Can we keep the runtime segment to 15m and surface two short demos: 1) continuous batching behavior on mixed-length workloads, 2) KV cache priming and warm-up timeline? I'll prepare a 3-slide live-demo plan.
- Requesting that the Q&A block has at least 20 minutes; Atlas typically drills into SLO tails and mitigations.
- I'll upload the demo checklist and a small script we run in staging to reproduce tail cases to the Drive folder; please give me a heads-up if you want me to sanitize any internal IDs.

I'll be offline Mon-Tue mornings; if you get a calendar confirmation from Alice, I can prep the demo assets by EOD Tue.

- Jonas
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
